report.summary: All four UI failures are 5-second Playwright timeouts on requests that render /books, and they share one root cause: the app's seeded slow_list bug adds a random 0-8 s sleep to every book-list render, which regularly exceeds the 5 s limit set in tests/ui/conftest.py. Nothing here is a product regression that fails every time, so don't debug the tests first; first confirm whether BUGS=slow_list is set in the CI environment and turn it off for the UI job (or make the list endpoint fast), then rerun to confirm the failures disappear.

causes.title: Random 0-8 s delay in list_books (slow_list bug) exceeds the 5 s UI timeout
causes.explanation: With the slow_list seeded bug enabled, list_books() sleeps a random 0-8 seconds on every call. Every UI path that renders /books calls list_books: GET /books (books_page -> render_books), the register redirect to /books, and the add-book POST, which re-renders /books with a 422 error for an invalid year. The conftest sets page.set_default_timeout(5000), so any navigation or click that waits on that render fails whenever the random delay exceeds about 5 s (roughly 3 in 8 chance per render). The two Page.goto('/books') failures time out on the 'load' event. The two click failures time out on 'waiting for scheduled navigations to finish' after the POST. The outcome depends on chance, so the same code can pass on rerun. The passing test test_existing_user_can_log_in also submits the login form and lands on /books, which is consistent with this being intermittent rather than a hard break. The root cause is the app's timing behaviour under the slow_list bug, and the tests cannot fix it by themselves. The fix is to stop the UI job from enabling slow_list, or to make the app fast when it is not being tested for slowness.
evidence: app/main.py:12 docstring: "slow_list        random 0-8 s delay when listing books (flaky timing)"
app/main.py:159-161: def list_books(user_id): if "slow_list" in BUGS: time.sleep(random.uniform(0, 8))
app/main.py:264-270: render_books() calls list_books(user["id"]) on every /books render, including the 422 re-render used by books_add
app/main.py:311 and 350: register_submit and books_add redirect to /books after the POST, so the next page load pays the same delay
Failure 1 (test_added_book_is_listed): Page.goto: Timeout 5000ms exceeded. navigating to "http://127.0.0.1:64649/books", waiting until "load"
Failure 2 (test_book_created_through_api_shows_in_ui): Page.goto: Timeout 5000ms exceeded. navigating to "http://127.0.0.1:64646/books", waiting until "load"

Failure 3 (test_new_user_lands_on_empty_bookshelf): Locator.click: Timeout 5000ms exceeded. ... click action done / waiting for scheduled navigations to finish (POST /register then redirect to /books)
Failure 4 (test_future_year_shows_error_and_keeps_input): Locator.click: Timeout 5000ms exceeded. ... click action done / waiting for scheduled navigations to finish (POST /books re-renders /books)
Other UI tests in the same run (e.g. test_existing_user_can_log_in) also reach /books and passed, which fits intermittent timing rather than a consistent defect.

Not verified: the CI environment variables (BUGS) are not visible from the workflow file .github/workflows/tests.yml, which does not set BUGS. The slow_list hypothesis relies on the env used by this run having it enabled; the failure timing (exactly the 5 s limit) strongly supports it.
causes.suggested_fix: First, check the environment of the UI job and make sure BUGS does not include slow_list for the normal UI suite. If the slow behaviour is meant to be tested, put that check in its own test that sets its own timeout, and keep the default suite fast. Second, as a stopgap, raise the page timeout for the UI suite (or allow a longer goto/click timeout only for /books-touching tests). Third, consider making the test harness start the app with BUGS explicitly cleared in tests/conftest.py base_url so local and CI runs behave the same. Then rerun the UI suite several times to confirm stability.
